html:
Eswatini has had the highest rate of HIV infection in the world, with over a quarter of adults living with the virus in the 2000s and 2010s.

The epidemic spread fast in the 1990s, helped by migrant labour, poverty and the movement of workers to South African mines. By the early 2000s life expectancy had fallen sharply, and many children lost their parents.

Free antiretroviral treatment from the mid 2000s, with foreign aid, changed the picture. By the late 2010s Eswatini was among the first countries to reach the targets set by the United Nations for testing and treatment, and new infections fell. It is part of the wider AIDS epidemic in Africa, under the rule of Mswati III.
sum: Eswatini has had the highest rate of HIV infection in the world, with over a quarter of adults living with the virus in the 2000s and 2010s.
